text:
olivia: Heads-up — started a quick triage on a regression hitting p95 on host-side parse. Observed microbursts (~10-30 reqs) that spike CPU in the parsing thread and immediately cause KV cache churn. Flamegraph attached in Gist, short summary below.

sam: Thanks. Is this during steady load or when we hit small concurrent bursts?

olivia: Small concurrent bursts, usually short payloads (~200-600 bytes). Not heavy decoding cost, it's the request framing + tokenize path. pprof shows `parse_request` and `stream_chunker` dominating for the 90th-99th percentiles.

raj: Any correlation with kernel selection / batching thresholds? Could be we fall back to slow kernel when sequence length distribution flips.

olivia: Good call — I toggled the kernel-picker trace. On these bursts the runtime switches to the generic AVX fallback because estimated batch size is < 4 and seq len variance is high. That fallback has higher per-token overhead, and combined with parsing cost it busts the KV TTL heuristics.

chen: Do we have a minimal repro? I can run a looped client hitting ingress with bursts to reproduce locally. Also want to capture KV cache evict traces.

olivia: Yep repro script (quick):

```
# repro client (bash)
for i in {1..500}; do
  seq 10 | xargs -n1 -P20 curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}';
  sleep 0.08
done
```

Works ~95% to reproduce the microburst.

denise: If KV evictions are happening, that explains tail amplification. We saw a similar pattern before where small-batch fallback + frequent small requests caused KVCACHE to prematurely evict hot prefixes. On that incident we adjusted cache TTL + sampling weight.

sam: What do the traces show for slice sizes and writev syscalls? I recall HTTP/gRPC framer was doing extra small writes which increases syscall overhead.

olivia: Correct — host-side framer emits many ~256B writes when streaming chunking is enabled. writev is called ~3x more often per response under the fallback kernel. Combined latency HRT shows syscall overhead adds ~120us per request.

raj: Two-pronged mitigation: 1) prevent kernel fallback for these microbursts by adjusting the batching heuristic threshold (lower the min-batch to 2 and prefer the optimized kernel when seq_len < 128). 2) coalesce small writes in the framer: buffer up to 1KB or until EOS/timer. Thoughts?

chen: Both sounds reasonable. Coalescing is low-risk; we've got tests for streaming semantics. Kernel heuristic tweak needs perf testing for long seq cases.

denise: Also consider temporary KV-ttl bump during detected microburst windows (short window TTL increase to reduce churn). Perf-bot can run an A/B with traffic shaping.

perf-bot: Scheduling perf jobs: job-id=perf/5789-kernbatch. Running: kernel-heuristic-A (min_batch=2) vs baseline. Estimated runtime 45m.

olivia: I'll start a canary with framer coalesce patch on staging and land kernel-heuristic branch behind a flag. Will capture end-to-end p95, KV eviction rate, and syscall counts.

sam: Please add a quick telemetry metric for "fallback-kernel-reasons" so we can see triggers by per-route.

olivia: Added a TODO.

chen: I'll run the repro with tools to capture writev counts and kvcache eviction hooks. Will post results in this thread.

olivia: Thanks team. If we get clear wins from coalescing alone we can ship that fast (hotfix), then iterate on kernel heuristics and TTL tuning. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: job perf/5789-kernbatch completed. Result summary: - kernel-heuristic-A: p95 down 14% under burst load, KV-evictions down 42%. Full logs in perf dashboard.

sam: Nice! Can we merge the coalesce hotfix now and leave kernel heuristic behind a runtime flag for a slow rollout?

olivia: Yep — will open PRs: coalesce hotfix (urgent), kernel-heuristic (flagged). PRs will reference this thread and perf job id.

chen: Posted writev/evict traces: writev calls reduced by ~60% after coalesce; syscall latency tail narrowed.

denise: Great work. Postmortem follow-up: add automated detection for this pattern (microburst + fallback kernel + writev storm) so we can auto-suggest fixes.

olivia: Filed follow-up (ENG-OPT-142). Closing triage for now unless someone sees regressions in long sequences.
